_comment: THE DAILY ROTA. One post per PROFILE per day, drawn from content/posts/.
The real file (content/daily_accounts.json) is GITIGNORED — it names real
accounts. This is the shape, committed so the format is documented.
A LIST, and they go out in ONE upload call. The duplicate-content pattern
that trips spam detection is the same clip on two accounts of the SAME
platform — not one account's Reel also appearing on its own TikTok, which is
what every creator does. So two clips a day covers four accounts.
A platform named here but not yet connected is SKIPPED with a notice, so
'tiktok' can sit in this file before the account exists.
false = the post publishes itself on the day. true = TikTok holds it in the
app's INBOX for you to finish (which is the only way to attach a trending
chart sound — those cannot be applied by any API, on any platform, ever).
⚠ INSTAGRAM HAS NO DRAFT STATE and ignores this: an IG upload is LIVE on
arrival either way. So draft:true on a profile that includes Instagram means
'IG posts itself, TikTok waits for me' — and if you never open the app, that
profile's TikTok never posts. Default false: a post that goes out with the
game's own music beats a draft sitting in an inbox.
⚠ THESE ARE LISTS BECAUSE A CONSTANT TEACHES NOTHING. Every post used to
carry the identical tags at the identical minute, so no amount of analytics
could say whether either helped — there was no contrast to measure. They
rotate by day index (deterministic, so a re-run picks the same one, and
balanced, so a month spreads evenly), and the variant is written into the
ledger at queue time. `insights.py` compares them once there are enough.
⚠ KEEP THE TWO CYCLE LENGTHS COPRIME. 3 tag sets against 3 times stay in
lockstep forever — tag set A is only ever seen at 09:12 — and the two
effects can then never be told apart. 3 against 4 takes 12 days to repeat
and covers every combination. That confound is built at config time and no
later analysis can undo it.
The three tag families below are deliberately DIFFERENT AUDIENCES rather
than reshuffles of the same words, so the comparison answers a question
worth asking: does this land better with animation people, gamedev people,
or general gaming? #stickspire is in all three as a constant anchor.
post_time is LOCAL (Europe/London); daily_post converts to a UTC instant.
Minutes deliberately avoid :00 and :30 — every scheduler on earth fires on
those, and the round number is a small bot tell.

_why: A SECOND ENTRY FOR THE SAME PROFILE = A SECOND UPLOAD CALL. One call carries
one `title`, so the strictest platform in it wins - putting YouTube in with
Instagram and TikTok would cap all three captions at YouTube's 100-character
TITLE limit. Current captions are 93 characters, so it fits today and would
silently start truncating on one longer matchup name.
same_clip_as: reuse the clip the flagship already took today, so YouTube costs
clip_suffix: the 9:16 cut from make_portrait.py. A LANDSCAPE upload to YouTube
is a normal video, not a Short, and gets no distribution. If the .portrait file
is missing the entry sits the day out rather than posting the wrong shape.
caption 'title': a title is one line. The two-line Instagram caption shape
extra.categoryId '20' is Gaming; the vendor defaults to '22' (People & Blogs).
extra.youtube_description is the only field on any of these platforms that can
carry a working link, so it carries the wishlist.
accounts.caption: title

extra.youtube_description:
STICKSPIRE is a stick-figure spell brawler about climbing a tower that keeps taking floors back. Nine classes, each with a signature spell.

Wishlist: https://stickspire.pages.dev

#Shorts #stickman #stickfight #indiegame #gamedev
